issues.legal_issue: After a person seeks a reference disputing compensation for acquired land, the Collector must provide the court with complete information about the acquired land.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the compensation award and applied for a reference to the court, seeking enhanced compensation for their land.
Their application and attached schedule did not identify every parcel by its recorded land number.
The Collector’s statement to the court included only the parcels listed in the schedule, although the award covered all of the landowners’ acquired land.
issues.conclusion: The Collector was required to send the court full information regarding the entire land acquired, including the particulars required for the reference; the acquiring authority could not rely on the landowners’ possible unfamiliarity with recorded parcel numbers.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 18 and 19 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a person who has not accepted the award may apply for a reference, including on the ground that compensation is inadequate. When making the reference, the Collector must provide the court with the information specified in Section 19(1), including the situation and extent of the land and particulars of trees, buildings, or crops. Once an application for reference is made, the Collector must provide full information concerning the entire land acquired. The Court relied on no earlier case for this principle.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A person whose land was acquired pursued a judicial reference concerning the acquisition award.
predicates.compensation_challenged: The person objected to the compensation awarded for the acquired land.
predicates.reference_application_filed: The person submitted a written application asking the relevant official to refer the matter to a court.

issues.definition: When a person pursues a judicial reference after challenging compensation for acquired land, the official making the reference must provide full information about all the acquired land.

issues.legal_issue: An application seeking enhanced compensation for all acquired land is not confined to the parcels itemized in an incomplete schedule when the application as a whole claims compensation for the entire acquisition.
material_facts: The landowners’ reference application stated that they sought enhanced compensation for the whole of their land, and its schedule ended with wording indicating that the listed parcels were not exhaustive.
The Collector’s statement omitted parcels covered by the acquisition award because they were not specifically listed in the schedule.
The landowners applied to the court for a direction requiring the Collector to provide a corrected statement covering all their acquired land.
The court at first instance directed the Collector to provide the corrected statement, but the High Court set that direction aside by treating the reference as limited to the listed parcels.
The landowners were not required to pay ad valorem court fees when applying to the Collector for a reference seeking enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The application sought enhanced compensation for the entire acquired land, not merely the parcels listed in the schedule. The court at first instance was justified in directing the Collector to furnish a correct statement, and the High Court’s order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of a reference application is determined by reading the application as a whole. Here, the claim for the whole land, the non-exhaustive wording of the schedule, and the absence of ad valorem court fees supported the conclusion that the claim was not limited to the listed parcels. Sections 18 and 19 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and Sections 151–153 of the Code of Civil Procedure were relevant to the reference and the request for a corrected statement. The Court considered it unnecessary to decide the matter through the High Court’s inquiry into counsel’s statement under Order X of the Code of Civil Procedure; it relied on no earlier case for its ruling.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference and application_claimed_entire_acquired_land and schedule_was_incomplete and collector_statement_omitted_acquired_land and correction_was_requested

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A person whose land was acquired pursued a judicial reference concerning the acquisition award.
predicates.application_claimed_entire_acquired_land: The reference application, read as a whole, sought enhanced compensation for all the land covered by the acquisition.
predicates.schedule_was_incomplete: The schedule attached to the application listed some parcels but indicated that the list was not exhaustive.
predicates.collector_statement_omitted_acquired_lan: The statement sent to the court left out parcels covered by the acquisition award.
predicates.correction_was_requested: The claimant asked the court to require the official who prepared the reference statement to correct it.

issues.definition: When a reference application claims enhanced compensation for all acquired land despite an incomplete schedule, and the reference statement omits some acquired land, the court may direct that the statement be corrected to cover all the acquired land.
